chunks.heading: What Are Your Surgical Options For Gum Disease Treatments?
chunks.text: In complex cases, non-surgical gum disease treatments like scaling or root planing may not be sufficient in restoring the gum health. chunks.title: Gum Disease Treatment Effective Gum Disease Treatment
chunks.heading: Gum Lifting
chunks.text: Gum lifting is a precision-led dental treatment procedure that repositions the gums to better protect your teeth. It involves gently folding back the gum tissue and deep cleaning around the roots of your teeth. After the thorough cleaning, we reposition the gum tissue securely, reducing the risk of future infection. To ensure the best possible comfort and outcome, this treatment is best performed by an experienced dentist.

chunks.title: Gum Disease Treatment Effective Gum Disease Treatment
chunks.heading: Gum Grafting
chunks.text: Gum Grafting as a gum disease treatment restores the areas that have been severely affected by gum disease. It involves rebuilding the lost gum tissue and protecting vulnerable tooth roots. Using healthy tissue that is often taken from the roof of your mouth, Shellharbour dentists attach it to the affected area to restore gum coverage. This treatment might be suitable for patients who have significant gum recession. Gum grafting shields the sensitive roots while preventing further bone and tissue loss. chunks.heading: Diamond solution (most recommended)
chunks.text: Dental implants provide the look and feel of natural teeth and can last for years, without needing to be repaired or replaced. With implants, you won’t need to limit yourself to what foods you can eat. And unlike dentures, you won’t have to worry about removing your implants.

chunks.title: Dental Implants Need Dental Implants? Visit Shellharbour Dentists
chunks.heading: Diamond solution (most recommended)
chunks.text: All-On-4 Dental Implants is a type of dental implant treatment that is designed to provide patients with a full set of new teeth in a single day. All-On-4 utilises just four dental implants placed in strategic positions to support a full arch of replacement teeth. This innovative approach results in a more time-efficient, and less invasive dental implant solution that can be used to restore an entire arch of missing or damaged teeth.

chunks.title: Dental Implants Need Dental Implants? Visit Shellharbour Dentists
chunks.heading: Implant-Retained dentures
chunks.text: Implant-retained dentures are a type of denture that is supported by dental implants, rather than relying solely on the gums for stability. The implants are surgically placed into the jawbone, and the denture is attached to the implants using special connectors. This provides a secure and comfortable fit, without the need for messy adhesives. Implant-retained dentures also help to preserve the jawbone, which can deteriorate over time when natural teeth are lost. chunks.heading: What is a Porcelain Veneer?
chunks.text: Porcelain veneers are thin, custom-made shells that are designed to cover the front surface of teeth. Our dentists attempt to create porcelain veneers that closely match the colour and shape of your natural teeth. These dental appliances are custom-made in an Australian dental laboratory and then carefully bonded to the teeth by Shellharbour Dentists. More information on the laboratory can be found here.

chunks.text: Porcelain veneers are modern dental appliances with many advantages. They can be considered if you: Have teeth that appear chipped, worn, or uneven. Have teeth with visible or older fillings that impact the smile’s overall appearance. Wish to change the colour of teeth that do not respond well to whitening treatments. Would like to improve the appearance of mild gaps or irregularly shaped teeth. Prefer a more durable alternative to composite veneers. Before considering veneers, it is important to have a dental assessment. chunks.text:
Why is my tooth sore?
Toothaches are the human body’s way of telling you that something is wrong. This could be a cracked tooth, a dental cavity, an exposed tooth root or even gum disease. We recommend that you schedule an appointment with us as soon as possible if you happen to be experiencing tooth pain. We have emergency appointments available every day, so call us on (02) 4284 4486 or Book online

chunks.title: Home
chunks.heading: What should I do if I get a tooth knocked out?
chunks.text:
What should I do if I get a tooth knocked out?
If a tooth is knocked out, you should pick it up by the crown and rinse it in milk. If milk is unavailable have the person who lost the tooth clean it with his/her saliva being careful not to scrape or touch the root of the tooth if possible. Carefully orient the tooth (so it is facing the right way) and carefully push it back into the socket. If you are unable to do this wrap the tooth in cling film. Either way immediately make your way to a dentist. Getting to a dentist quickly is critical if the tooth is to be saved, we leave always room for Dental Emergencies.

chunks.text:
How can I improve my oral hygiene?
In order to keep your teeth and gums healthy, we encourage flossing and daily brushing to maintain proper hygiene. Using mouthwashes, cleaning your tongue and eating a healthy diet which limits sugary food and soft drinks can also help. We also recommend regular visit to a dentist for a comprehensive oral assessment at least once in 6 months.

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: Teeth Grinding Woonona – All You Need to Know
chunks.text: Do you suffer from teeth grinding? Woonona patients aren’t always aware that they have this problem until they visit their dentist for a regular check-up, or until their partner complains of being kept awake at night with the noise they’re making.

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: What is teeth grinding and what causes it?
chunks.text: Teeth grinding, or bruxism as it’s also referred to, is the involuntary clenching and grinding of the teeth. It happens predominantly at night when a person is asleep, although it can also happen during the day. While stress and anxiety are cited as being the main causes, a person may also grind their teeth when they’re concentrating, if their teeth are misaligned, or even as a side effect of antidepressants. Did you know that around 5% of the Australian population are already struggling with this issue?

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: The dangers of teeth grinding
chunks.text: Teeth grinding is bad for your smile because it causes: ● Wear and tear to tooth enamel● Damage to restorations● Cracked teeth● Tooth sensitivity● Gum recession● Strain to the TMJ● Enlarged cheek muscles The good news is that we can help protect your teeth from further damage with the mouthguards our Woonona dentists design, and we can discuss ways of helping you to address this problem.

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: How to know if you grind your teeth
chunks.text: Are you one of the many people in Woonona that grind their teeth? You may be if you’ve noticed any of the following symptoms: ● Your jaw feels tender and sore when you awake in the morning● Your teeth appear shorter and flatter● Recession of your gums has exposed the yellow tooth roots● You wake with a headache most mornings If you’re not sure whether you grind your teeth, then schedule a visit with our friendly and experienced dentists. They’ve got over 4 decades of experience among them in restoring patients’ smiles and helping prevent teeth grinding in Woonona.

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: Teeth grinding treatment
chunks.text: There are many treatments available for teeth grinding, including relaxation techniques such as meditation and yoga. If your teeth grinding is related to anger or anxiety, you may want to consider talking through your problems with a counsellor. Some people find that taking more exercise or going for long walks helps relax them and improves sleep, which in turn may stop them from grinding their teeth. If your bite is misaligned, our dentist may recommend orthodontic treatment to put an end to your problem. We may not be able to stop your teeth grinding habit, but we can recommend a custom mouthguard which is worn over the upper teeth. This cushions your teeth from the bite force and means that the mouthguard takes the brunt of your grinding instead of your tooth enamel.

chunks.title: Teeth Grinding
chunks.heading: Sports mouthguards
chunks.text: Besides teeth grinding, mouthguards can be useful for sport lovers. The risk of contact to the face and teeth is an ever-present danger in some sports. To minimise this risk, it’s a good idea to wear a mouthguard. Mouthguards are usually worn during sports and other activities that involve a high risk of impact to the face. According to the Australian Dental Association (ADA), about one-third of traumatic injuries to teeth are sports-related. Sports Medicine Association Australia suggests that 50% of children experience some form of dental injury. A custom mouthguard might prove far better than any generic mouthguard you can purchase from a store, so if you grind your teeth and you’d like a mouthguard made for you, then book an appointment with our dentists. Call Woonona Dentists today on (02) 4284 4486.

chunks.title: Gum Disease Treatment
chunks.heading: But what is gum disease? Our Woonona dental team explain…
chunks.text: By “Gum disease” we mean the inflammation of the gum line, which in advanced stages may also affect the jawline bone supporting the teeth. Gum disease is identified in three stages, and Woonona patients should be informed about them. These are: Gingivitis Periodontitis Advanced periodontitis The stages are presented here by order of severity, meaning that gingivitis is the first stage, while advanced periodontitis is the most advanced stage of the disease. The recommended course of action differs according to the stage. Gingivitis can be treated relatively easily, using professional dental cleaning techniques which remove tartar build up. Periodontitis and advanced periodontitis on the other hand need more focused attention. In case a patient with gingivitis doesn’t get treatment, toxins from bacterial plaque will build up and start to affect the gum tissue and the ligaments and bone tissue that are supporting the teeth. If the disease advances that far, there are treatment options both surgical and non-surgical.

chunks.text: After scaling and root planing, if remaining gum tissue isn’t properly jointed with the tooth, maybe plaque will slowly gather in the pockets causing further damage. To tackle this issue, we might propose to patient to undergo periodontal pocket reduction surgery. Despite the big name, it’s a relatively simple process, in which the gum tissue is folded back, the root thoroughly cleaned, and the gum reattached, so it fits snugly.

chunks.title: Gum Disease Treatment
chunks.heading: Gum Grafting
chunks.text: In some cases, if gum disease has advanced and corroded the gum, exposing the highly sensitive tooth roots, our recommended gum disease treatment in Woonona would be gum graft. In this process, gum is taken from some other area of the mouth (mainly the palate) and is then attached like a flap to cover the exposed tooth or teeth. chunks.title: Wisdom Teeth Removal
chunks.heading: So why do wisdom teeth need to be removed in the first place?
chunks.text: Wisdom teeth, otherwise known as third molars, are usually the last to erupt. While some people have no problems with their wisdom teeth, a good many others will. The fact is that in the modern world, our third molars aren’t really needed and because they’re located at the very back of the mouth, often, there simply isn’t enough room for them to grow. Even for those people who have good oral health, when wisdom teeth problems arise, a dentist may recommend removal. It’s not unusual for wisdom teeth to be positioned crookedly or even sideways and will usually be spotted during a routine dental check-up. When this happens they can cause problems to adjacent teeth, so wisdom tooth extraction is the best option.

chunks.title: Wisdom Teeth Removal
chunks.heading: How does the tooth extraction process work for Wonoona dental patients?
chunks.text: During a consultation, our dental team at Woonona will go over your medical and dental history. Next, if it’s a simple non-impacted tooth extraction, the area will be numbed with anaesthetic and the wisdom tooth will be gently removed. Patients should feel no pain during the procedure as the area is numbed but may feel some slight pressure. The whole process should be over in a few minutes. After extraction, our Woonona team will give you aftercare instructions including medications to take if you do feel any pain. For more complex wisdom tooth extractions, Woonona Dentists have a visiting expert, Dr. Pat Pandey who is highly experienced in complex wisdom teeth removal. Extraction procedures can be carried out under either a local or general anaesthetic or IV sedation. As such, when it comes to simple or impacted wisdom teeth removal, Woonona dentists can deal with most types of teeth extractions and do it at affordable rates. If you have a complicated medical background or if the wisdom teeth are too close to the nerve, then we will refer you to our trusted specialist.

chunks.title: Tooth Fillings
chunks.heading: Tooth Fillings in Woonona – Restorative Dentistry at Woonona Dentists
chunks.text: If you are in need of tooth fillings in Woonona, then we’re here to help. Dental fillings are necessary when a tooth is showing signs of decay, or a cavity has developed. Here at Woonona Dentists we use high quality natural looking composite fillings as an alternative to old style silver amalgam fillings, because we want to work in a mercury free environment.

chunks.title: Tooth Fillings
chunks.heading: The procedure for composite dental fillings
chunks.text: First, any decay (or the old amalgam filling) is removed, and our dentist shapes the cavity and rough edges. A good quality bonding liquid is applied to help the filling adhere to the tooth structure. A composite material, colour matched to your natural teeth for a seamless finish, is applied inside the cavity in thin layers. A special blue light is used to cure each layer. Once the cavity is filled with the composite material, the restoration is shaped and polished at the margins and on the surface, to prevent food trappings and maintain an even bite.

chunks.title: Tooth Fillings
chunks.heading: Composite (white) dental fillings in Woonona have their advantages:
chunks.text: They’re highly aesthetic and natural looking They allow for minimal shrinkage They don’t contain traces of mercury They can be used on front and back teeth They can be completed in just one dental visit

chunks.title: Tooth Fillings
chunks.heading: Ceramic inlays or indirect fillings
chunks.text: Ceramic inlays, also known as indirect fillings, normally require two visits to our dental clinic because they’re manufactured at a 100% Australian dental laboratory. Ceramic inlays are usually recommended when the tooth structure is not considered strong enough to support a filling, but isn’t so weak that it requires a dental crown. Our dentist will remove any decay from your tooth, and then take a digital impression which records the shape of the tooth that’s being repaired and the teeth surrounding it. A temporary filling is put in place to protect the tooth while the dental lab sets about making your custom indirect filling/porcelain crown. During the second visit, your temporary filling is removed, and our dentist checks the fit of the crown/cap. If you and our dentist are happy with the fit, then it will be cemented firmly in place. Best of all, as we use 100% Australian Lab, the crowns comes with up to 15 years Warranty!

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.heading: Crowns and Bridges in Woonona – Restore Your Smile Beautifully
chunks.text: Damaged or missing teeth can mark your smile and put a dent in your confidence and, if you just ignore the situation, things are likely to get worse. Fortunately, we can treat both of these dental problems with crowns or bridges in Woonona, and get your oral health, confidence and smile back on track. Let’s take a look at the difference between crowns and bridges.

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.heading: What is a dental crown?
chunks.text: A dental crown is a cap which covers the visible part of a tooth which sits above the gumline. Our Woonona dentists use crowns in a variety of ways, to: Restoring a tooth that is broken or worn Hold a bridge in place (dental crowns sit on the adjacent supporting teeth) Protect and strengthen a tooth following a root canal Strengthen a tooth with minimal structure remaining Cover a misshapen or discoloured tooth Top a dental implant

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.heading: What is a dental bridge?
chunks.text: Fixed bridges in Woonona are one way we can replace missing teeth. A bridge is made by covering the teeth on either side of the space with crowns, and then joining them together with a false tooth or teeth in the middle to cover the gap.

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.heading: Once in position a dental bridge can:
chunks.text: Close a gap left by a missing tooth or teeth Improve bite function and chewing ability Prevent existing teeth from drifting into spaces Support facial structures in order to retain facial shape Provide a fixed and long term option, compared to a removable denture

chunks.title: Crowns and Bridges
chunks.heading: How are crowns and bridges made?
chunks.text: Before either a crown or bridge is made, the tooth/teeth will have to be prepared to accommodate the crown or bridge. After preparing the teeth, our dentist will take a digital impression to create an exact model for the dental lab to craft your crown or bridge. If porcelain is being used for crowns and bridges, our Woonona dentists will choose a shade closest to your natural teeth. You’ll be fitted with ‘temporaries’ until your custom crowns and bridges have been made. To complete the procedure, your permanent crowns and/or bridges are checked for fit, and permanently cemented in place. As all our crowns and bridges are made Australia, they come with up to 15 years warranty! If you’re looking to restore your smile, then give Woonona Dentists a call on (02) 4284 4486 to schedule a consultation. Our high-quality crowns and bridges are available with a lab guarantee, depending on the materials used, please ask our dentist for more information prior to treatment.

chunks.title: Dentures
chunks.heading: Dentures at Woonona Dentists
chunks.text: If you have lost your natural teeth due to damage, decay or injury, dentures can replace your missing teeth and restore your smile. Dentures offer a natural looking solution, enhancing your appearance and benefiting your health.

chunks.title: Dentures
chunks.heading: Missing Teeth
chunks.text: Missing teeth can cause the facial muscles to droop, causing a person to look older than they actually are. With the support from dentures, you will appear youthful while being able to enjoy food and speak comfortably, just as if you still had your natural teeth. Dentures are removable false teeth that are worn to replace missing teeth. These artificial teeth are generally made of acrylic and designed to best match your natural teeth. The base of a denture is called a plate and is usually made of either acrylic or metal. Dentures can be taken out and put back into the mouth, and they are available as either full or partial dentures, depending on how many teeth need to be restored. Today’s dentures are natural looking and more comfortable than ever. At Woonona dentists, we offer Implant-supported dentures as a permanent alternative to traditional dentures.

chunks.title: Root Canal Treatment
chunks.heading: Root Canal Treatment – Woonona Dentists
chunks.text: When the pulp inside one of your teeth becomes infected or injured root canal treatment could save the tooth from extraction. During this treatment the dentist will remove the diseased pulp, file and clean the canals of the tooth and anti-bacterial medicines are placed inside the canal. It usually takes 2-3 visits and x-rays help show the progress and success of the treatment. Once it has been determined that the treatment has been successful, a permanent porcelain crown or filling will be placed to seal the tooth.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: Dental Implants in Woonona – A Permanent Solution to Tooth Loss
chunks.text: Are you considering dental implants in Woonona? Dental implants have revolutionised the dental industry, and provide a permanent long- lasting solution to tooth loss. Whether you’re missing one or more teeth, or all of your teeth, we can restore your smile and bite functionality, using dental implants in a variety of ways.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: What are dental implants exactly?
chunks.text: Dental implants are used to support one or more false teeth, and act as replacement tooth roots. They’re made from titanium, which is lightweight and strong and, since this metal is biocompatible, isn’t rejected by the body. Instead, over a period of 3 to 6 months, the surrounding bone and soft tissues fuse with it, so it becomes a permanent fixture in the mouth. Once this has happened, the implant(s) can be topped with a single crown or dental bridge, or stabilise dentures and prevent them from becoming loose. Here at Woonona Dentists we use high quality implant brands from leading manufacturers including MIS, Southern Implants, and Straumann, which have proved to be successful and reliable over many years.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: Consultation
chunks.text: As in any dental procedure, we need you to attend a consultation in order to determine whether dental implants are a suitable restoration solution for you. Using the latest intraoral cameras and digital X-rays including CBCT scan referral, we’ll determine whether you have sufficient bone density to support the implants. In some cases, our dentist will recommend a bone graft prior to dental implants, to increase the width and depth of bone in the implant area.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: First Appointment
chunks.text: Our visiting implantologist dentist, Dr Chin Valsan will place your dental implants chairside. He can also use IV sedation if you’re a nervous patient – but you do not need to have IV sedation for this procedure. Prior in-depth planning using 3-D computer technology allows for a shorter surgery time and more accurate placement. The gums will be opened up and the implant/s placed. Once this is done, the gums are sutured, and you’ll be sent home to recover. The actual implant placement usually takes less than 30 minutes!

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: Second Appointment
chunks.text: Once the dental implants have fused with the bone in a process known as osseointegration, you’ll need a second visit to assess the stability of the dental implant and to take an impression for the dental crown(s) or bridge.This will be done by Dr. Beena Kurian, our experienced Principal Dentist.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: Third Appointment
chunks.text: During this appointment, the crown(s) or bridge are screwed/cemented firmly in place to the stable implant, and the restoration is completed. Depending on the individual patient situation, the dental implant procedure takes from 3 to 9 months to complete.

chunks.title: Dental Implants
chunks.heading: What are the benefits of dental implants?
chunks.text: Dental implants put a halt to the bone loss which naturally occurs when a tooth is lost. While replacing teeth, dental implants also help preserve the jaw, maintaining its shape and density The facial structures are supported and indirectly, the soft tissues, gums, cheeks, and lips are too Bite functionality is restored, meaning a person can eat all of their favourite foods as they used to before Dental implants are easy to maintain by brushing and flossing, as you would do for your natural teeth Dental implants feel, look, and act like natural teeth If you’d like more information about dental implants in Woonona, or want to find out whether you’re a suitable candidate, why not call Woonona Dentists, today on (02) 4284 4486 for a FREE implant consultation? Disclaimer: Any surgical or invasive procedure carries risks. Before proceeding, you should seek a second opinion from an appropriately qualified health practitioner.

chunks.title: IV Sedation
chunks.heading: Is everyone a suitable candidate for IV sedation?
chunks.text: If you’re interested in having dental treatments carried out under conscious sedation, then you’ll be asked first to attend a short consultation. Your will also asked to fill out an online questionnaire, which will give the sedationist an opportunity to determine whether IV sedation is the most effective pain and anxiety relieving option for you or whether it would be more advisable to have treatment under a general anaesthetic under the care of a qualified anaesthetist. If it’s decided that IV sedation treatment is suitable for you, then you will be required to follow some very important instructions: You must bring an adult with you to the dental clinic who can stay while you undergo treatment and drive you home afterwards It can take up to 24 hours for the medication to leave your body. During that time, you must not drink any alcohol and it’s wise to stay home and rest You must not drive or use any heavy machinery for 24 hours after the procedure

chunks.title: IV Sedation
chunks.heading: IV Sedation – Do’s and Don’ts
chunks.text: Wear loose fitting comfortable clothes Brush your teeth thoroughly before your appointment Continue to take your regular medication with a small sip of water, unless we tell you otherwise Do Not Eat or drink anything for 6 hours prior to your appointment Do Not Attend your appointment if you’ve been unwell 2 weeks prior to your appointment. Instead, ring and cancel and we’ll reschedule it. Do Not Smoke for 24 hours prior to your schedule appointment Do Not Wear contact lenses, nail polish or jewellery during your appointment If you’d like to know more about IV sedation in Woonona or whether it’s a suitable option for you, then please get in touch with Woonona Dentists by calling (02) 4284 4486. Don’t avoid going to the dentists – we’re here to help!

chunks.title: Porcelain Veneers
chunks.heading: What is a porcelain veneer?
chunks.text: They’re thin shells of porcelain which cover the teeth a little like a false nail covers a fingernail. They fit to the front of your teeth and are colour-matched to your natural teeth for a seamless finish. Unlike dental veneers that are made from composite and are sculpted onto the tooth by our dentist, porcelain veneers are made in a 100% Australian dental laboratory and cemented in place.

chunks.title: Porcelain Veneers
chunks.heading: What can porcelain veneers be used for?
chunks.text: Porcelain veneers are extremely versatile and can be the perfect solution for: Badly stained or coloured teeth Crooked or misshapen teeth Chipped, cracked, or broken teeth Gaps between teeth Visible fillings which appear unattractive As in all our cosmetic treatments, we ask that you attend a consultation whereby our dentists can assess your oral health and dental needs, to determine if dental veneers are the best solution for you.

chunks.title: Porcelain Veneers
chunks.heading: Why choose porcelain over composite veneers?
chunks.text: Porcelain has a similar translucency to that of teeth enamel, and therefore looks more natural. In addition, it’s stronger and more durable, and less likely to stain than composite veneers. In fact, our porcelain veneers are available with a lab guarantee of up to 15 years, but please speak to our dentist prior to treatment about the exact fees involved and warranty.

chunks.title: Porcelain Veneers
chunks.heading: What’s the procedure for porcelain veneers?
chunks.text: In most cases a small layer of tooth enamel will need to be removed from your teeth, using anaesthetic if necessary, so that the veneer will fit flush with your other teeth. Once this has been done, our dentist takes a digital impression of the tooth and surrounding gums and teeth so that your custom veneer can be crafted. If necessary, you’ll be fitted with a temporary veneer until we call you back for your second appointment. During the second appointment, your permanent veneers will be checked and adjusted for fit before being bonded firmly in place.

chunks.title: Porcelain Veneers
chunks.heading: Are porcelain veneers right for you?
chunks.text: While porcelain veneers can disguise a number of dental problems, they’re not suitable for everyone. If you’re considering getting porcelain veneers in Woonona, then why not come and talk to the expert team at Woonona Dentists? Call us today on (02) 4284 4486 to book your appointment. We love helping patients get the beautiful smile they deserve.

A new filling or crown will be needed so visit Woonona Dental Clinic as soon as you can for a solution.

chunks.title: Dental Emergencies

chunks.text: There are simple precautions to help prevent certain injuries to the teeth. When participating in sport or recreational activities, always wear a custom-made mouthguard that is designed and fitted by a dentist. When opening a pack of chips, a bag of peanuts or other plastic containers of food products, always use scissors rather that your teeth.

chunks.title: Teeth Whitening
chunks.heading: Teeth Whitening Woonona Dentists Recommend
chunks.text: Don’t despair if your teeth aren’t gleaming white. We’re here to help you achieve a brighter, whiter smile. With professional teeth whitening in Woonona, you’ll soon be beaming all over your face! Our experienced dentists use Philips Zoom teeth whitening in Woonona, because it delivers exceptional results, and is sufficiently versatile to meet most of our patients’ dental needs.

chunks.title: Teeth Whitening
chunks.heading: Teeth whitening in Woonona your way
chunks.text: Patients considering Philips Zoom teeth whitening in Woonona can choose from Chair-side or at-home options. To ensure best results it is strongly recommend that you have a check-up and clean first to assess your oral health and ensure there is no plaque or tartar present that can affect the whitening treatment.

chunks.title: Teeth Whitening
chunks.heading: Chair-side whitening
chunks.text: If you need quick result under the guidance of our dentist, then we recommend in-chair whitening using Philips Zoom. The procedure takes no more than an hour, and can whiten your teeth by up to 8 shades. Before the procedure gets underway, your lips and gums are covered leaving just your teeth exposed. The whitening gel is carefully applied to the teeth, and a Zoom light is shone on them. This helps the hydrogen peroxide-based gel penetrate the surface of the teeth, breaking down any stains and discolouration. After 15 minutes, the gel is wiped away and the procedure is repeated twice more, for a treatment time of 45 minutes. $650 chair-side Philips Zoom teeth whitening (Valued at $850) – It is quick, convenient, safe, effective!

chunks.title: Teeth Whitening
chunks.heading: At-home whitening
chunks.text: For patients who are looking for a less-expensive alternative, and are happy to adopt a slower approach to teeth whitening, we recommend our Philips Zoom take-home bleaching kits. You’ll be issued with customised whitening trays to ensure a good fit and prevent the gel from touching your gums or soft tissues. We’ll also provide you with the Philips Zoom whitening gel, and give you directions for usage. Typically, you’ll wear your trays overnight for around 2 weeks, so your teeth whiten as you sleep. While you may not achieve quite the same level of whiteness as chair-side procedure, the treatment will still leave your teeth noticeably brighter. Only $450 for Custom Tray and Whitening Materials! chunks.text: We’re excited to welcome new patients with genuine care, open communication, and a calm environment designed to help you feel at ease from the start.

chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: Helping New Patients Feel Comfortable From Their Very First Appointment
chunks.text: We understand visiting a new dentist can feel unfamiliar or even a little daunting. That’s why we take the time to listen, explain each step, and create a calm, welcoming experience from day one. Your first appointment is an opportunity to ask questions, share your concerns, and feel genuinely cared for. We’ll review your health history, discuss your goals, and support you every step of the way.

chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: Health Fund Members Welcome, and Claims Made Easy
chunks.text: Bring your health fund card, and we’ll process claims on the spot, making your visit simpler, quicker, and more convenient.

chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: What Happens at Your Appointment
chunks.text: Know what to expect—gentle care at every stage of your appointment, from start to finish. You’ll be welcomed by our team and asked about your dental and medical history. This helps us understand your needs, preferences, and priorities before starting your examination or discussing personalised treatment options. Your dentist will carefully examine your teeth, gums, and bite to assess your overall oral health. If necessary, X-rays will be taken to gain a clearer view of areas not visible during the visual exam. A professional dental cleaning may also be included to remove plaque and tartar buildup. Throughout the appointment, we’ll clearly explain each step so you feel informed, at ease, and fully comfortable. After your exam, we’ll take the time to explain our findings, discuss any recommended treatments, and answer your questions. You’ll be fully supported in understanding your options and making informed decisions about your dental care.

chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.text: Answers to common questions about our New Patient Offer—what’s included, who it’s for, and how your dental visit will work. The New Patient Offer is designed to be affordable. You may not have any out-of-pocket costs if your health fund includes dental cover and your available limits have not been exceeded. If your appointment isn’t covered, the full offer is available for a capped fee of $250. We can process any eligible health fund claims on the spot using your card at the time of your visit. You may be eligible for our gap-free offer if you are a health fund member and meet the applicable criteria. Eligibility depends on factors such as your level of cover and available limits, which determine whether your appointment can be fully covered with no out-of-pocket expense. To be eligible, the following must apply: You have private health fund cover that includes general dental services. This type of cover will include dental check-ups, cleans, fluoride treatments, and other preventive care.

The full appointment is available for a capped fee of $250 when dental cover isn’t included, or your limits have been reached. chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.text: Our team will guide you through your treatment options, current fees, and available payment options to help you plan your next visit with confidence. Preparing a few important items before your first dental appointment is helpful. It allows us to provide safe, efficient, and personalised care from the moment you arrive. It also helps us gather the information needed to make your visit as smooth and productive as possible. Health fund card: If you have a health fund that includes dental cover, bringing your card allows us to process your claim on the spot. This can reduce or eliminate out-of-pocket costs, depending on your level of cover and remaining limits. List of current medications: Some medications may affect your oral health, healing response, or the suitability of certain treatments. A current list helps your dentist make safe and appropriate treatment decisions, especially if prescriptions or anaesthetics are involved. Medical history details: Understanding your general health is an important part of providing dental care.

While not required, bringing them can help your dentist assess changes in your oral health more accurately. Questions or concerns: Your first visit is a great opportunity to ask about any dental concerns, treatment goals, or preferences. Whether you’re feeling uncertain about dental care or planning future treatment, we’re here to listen and support you without pressure. Bringing these items allows us to provide care that’s efficient and tailored to you. If you’re not sure what to bring or have any questions before your appointment, feel free to contact us. We’re here to help. Digital X-rays are a valuable diagnostic tool that gives your dentist a better view of your oral health.

chunks.title: New Patient Offer
chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.text: They help assess areas not visible during a dental check-up and provide a more complete understanding of your oral health, supporting safe and personalised care. Here’s how they’re typically used during your visit: Detect tooth decay between teeth: Some cavities develop in areas that can’t be seen with the eye alone. X-rays help us detect these issues early before they become more serious. Evaluate the health of supporting bone: X-rays give us a clear view of the bone structure around your teeth. This is especially important for identifying early signs of gum disease or bone loss. Monitor tooth and jaw development: For children, teens, or patients undergoing orthodontic treatment, X-rays provide valuable insights into tooth and jaw development. They help track how structures are forming, aligning, or changing over time. Identify underlying infections or root changes: Dental pain isn’t always obvious on the surface. X-rays help reveal problems at the root of a tooth that may be due to infection.
